context:
Goal: sessions question your rules when the facts call for it, instead of deferring to them.
Problem (rule): the check that refuses a repeat of a settled question also refuses a measured challenge to a past ruling, so changing that check needs your yes.
Based on (ruling): your 13:01 CST words "my rules are to be challenged/questioned and never read as absolutes given im imperfect", and 13:04 CST: the checks should flag deference "just like how it identifies when shared mistakes and other stuff happens".
Based on (read): the check that refuses a repeat of a settled question cannot tell a nag from a challenge.
Departs from: main refuses any question on a settled point — a challenge that brings the ruling's text, a measure, what the ruling protected and a fix passes; a repeat with no new fact is still refused; the check that reads replies flags one that names a flaw in a ruling but defers with no measure or fix.
Meanwhile: nothing changes until your yes; it is planned work after the fresh start.
home: the restart plan (its item on challenging past rulings); the decision on the one form every question to you takes; the rule on how a session challenges a stale ruling

options.gain: Sessions bring you measured challenges to your rules, and deference gets flagged.
options.how: A lane changes the check to pass a measured challenge, rewrites its refusal text, adds a test that proves both paths, and adds one flag to the check that reads replies.
options.label: Yes, build it (Recommended)
options.lose: Some questions on settled points reach you again, when they bring a new fact.

options.gain: No change to how questions are checked.
options.label: No
options.lose: Sessions keep deferring to rules they could challenge.

reply: You answered in chat at 13:10 CST (relayed by the retrospective): "yes on r39". A lane builds it after the fresh start: roadmap step ruling-challenge-passes.
short: Let sessions challenge your rules, and flag deference?
title: Should the checks let a session challenge a past ruling with a measure and a fix, and flag replies that defer?
why: The check that stops repeat questions also stops measured challenges.
